n: William Marks and Newel K. Whitney, leaders still in Kirtland, are told to settle their affairs and move to Missouri before winter. Many faithful Saints had already left the troubled Ohio community.

f.w: before I, the Lord, send again the snows

n: Three urgent verbs—awake, arise, come forth—stress that they must not delay.
Delay would bring them harm. Kirtland was no longer the gathering place.

f.w: it shall not be well with them

n: The Lord asks a famous question: “What is property unto me?” He created everything; clinging to possessions is a spiritual danger.

f.g: Strong desire for possessions, especially what belongs to others.

n: Let Kirtland property go to pay debts. Whatever remains, they may keep. Don’t let land hold you back from following God.

f.g: Sold or handed over to satisfy creditors.

n: God owns the birds, fish, beasts, and the earth itself, and he controls the fate of nations. He doesn’t need anyone’s land.

f.w: Have I not made the earth?

n: God can make empty, lonely places bloom and produce abundantly—so trust him for a new beginning.

f.w: make solitary places to bud and to blossom

n: There is plenty of room in Missouri, at Adam-ondi-Ahman and the plains of Olaha Shinehah, where Adam lived. Why covet a “drop” in Kirtland and miss weightier things?

f.g: A name for the plains near Adam-ondi-Ahman; “Shinehah” appears elsewhere as a name for the sun.

n: So come to Zion, the land of God’s people.

f.g: Here, the Saints’ gathering area in northern Missouri.

n: William Marks, if faithful in small things, will be given greater responsibility. He is to preside at Far West. He later served as stake president in Nauvoo.

Newel K. Whitney is rebuked for being caught up with a worldly group and for “littleness of soul.” He is to come to Adam-ondi-Ahman and be a bishop in deed, not just in name. He accepted the correction and served faithfully.

f.g: In Revelation, the Nicolaitans were a group in the early church condemned for compromising with worldliness; here, apostates and money-minded men in Kirtland.

n: Oliver Granger, a less prominent member, is singled out for praise: his name will be honored forever. The Lord sees faithfulness that the world overlooks.
Oliver Granger was assigned to settle the First Presidency’s debts in Kirtland. The Lord says even if he “falls” (fails), he will rise; his sacrifice matters more to God than his success.

f.w: his sacrifice shall be more sacred unto me than his increase
f.g: A key principle: God values faithful effort over measurable results.

n: He too should come to Zion, where he will act as a merchant for the Saints’ benefit.

f.g: An agent handling business on behalf of the Church.

n: No one should look down on Oliver Granger; the Saints should bless him forever.
The Saints remaining in Kirtland must keep the temple holy. The Lord will in his time “overthrow the moneychangers”—as Jesus cleansed the temple of those turning worship into profit.
